$comment: Behavior vectors for the Octonomy Go SDK's transport: what a client does with a response, and which of its own requests it refuses before sending. Language-neutral: inputs and outcomes are data, and each line's test binding maps a reason string to its own way of recognising it. See README.md in this directory.

response.name: single-resource
response.description: The floor case: a single resource under the data envelope decodes.

response.name: single-resource-accepted-not-ok
response.description: Any 2xx answers a single-resource call; 202 decodes as 200 does.

response.name: single-resource-empty-body
response.description: A 2xx with no body where a resource was expected. Decoding nothing into a resource yields a zero value; it must be an error.

response.name: single-resource-whitespace-body
response.description: A body of only whitespace is not empty: it is a JSON document with nothing in it.

response.name: single-resource-without-envelope
response.description: The bare resource the vendored spec describes and the server never sends. Decoding it as an envelope finds no data key (#32).

response.name: single-resource-data-null
response.description: The envelope is present and holds null where a resource belongs.

response.name: single-resource-data-empty-object
response.description: An empty object fills in nothing and would decode to a zero-valued resource (#40).

response.name: single-resource-data-empty-object-with-space
response.description: An empty object is empty however it is spaced.

response.name: single-resource-data-array
response.description: An array where one resource belongs -- the list shape answering a single-resource call.

response.name: single-resource-data-scalar
response.description: A scalar where one resource belongs.

response.name: single-resource-data-number
response.description: A number where one resource belongs.

response.name: single-resource-id-null
response.description: A non-empty object whose identity is null. The shape check passes it; only the identity check can refuse it.

response.name: single-resource-id-empty
response.description: An identity that is present and empty is as blank as one that is absent.

response.name: single-resource-id-renamed
response.description: The identity under a key the model does not read -- what a renamed field looks like to a decoder that ignores unknown keys.

response.name: single-resource-id-whitespace
response.description: Identity is checked for absence and emptiness, not trimmed: an id of only whitespace is present, and decodes as it was sent.

response.name: single-resource-field-wrong-type
response.description: A field of the resource carrying the wrong JSON type is refused, not decoded leniently.

response.name: single-resource-truncated-json
response.description: A body cut off mid-document.

response.name: list-page
response.description: The floor case for a list: rows under data, and a pagination block.

response.name: list-empty-page
response.description: An empty page is an answer, not an error.

response.name: list-data-null
response.description: A present-but-null data array means no rows, as [] does. Whether a binding exposes it as an empty or an absent collection is that line's own business; the vector pins only that no rows arrived.

response.name: list-without-data
response.description: A pagination block with no data key at all.

response.name: list-without-pagination
response.description: Rows with no pagination block. A missing block reads as one complete page to a caller paging on count.

response.name: list-pagination-null
response.description: A null pagination block is as missing as an absent one.

response.name: list-pagination-empty-object
response.description: A pagination block that is present and carries nothing decodes to a limit of 0. The server's paginator never sends a limit below 1.

response.name: list-pagination-limit-zero
response.description: An explicit limit of 0.

response.name: list-pagination-limit-zero-with-rows
response.description: An unusable limit is refused on a page that has rows, not only on an empty one.

response.name: list-pagination-wrong-type
response.description: A pagination value of the wrong JSON type.

response.name: list-data-wrong-type
response.description: An object where the rows array belongs.

response.name: list-row-null
response.description: A null row: the page length is right and the row is blank, which nobody inspects one row of fifty for.

response.name: list-row-empty-object
response.description: An empty-object row.

response.name: list-row-without-identity
response.description: A row that is a non-empty object with no identity.

response.name: list-row-field-wrong-type
response.description: A field of a row carrying the wrong JSON type.

response.name: delete-no-content
response.description: A delete (a deactivation, on the server) answered the way Octonomy answers every delete: 204 and no body.

response.name: delete-answered-with-a-payload
response.description: A 200 carrying a resource where a 204 belongs: the call reached something that is not the delete route it meant to, and succeeding would discard what it said.

response.name: delete-answered-with-an-empty-200
response.description: A 200 with no body. The status alone is not the one the delete contract names.

response.name: delete-answered-with-a-202
response.description: A 202 is a 2xx, and still not the 204 the delete contract names.

response.name: error-envelope-not-found
response.description: An Octonomy error envelope keeps the server's code, status and request id.

response.name: error-envelope-validation
response.description: A 400 validation envelope.

response.name: error-envelope-unknown-code
response.description: A code this vector file has never heard of is reported verbatim, not mapped to anything a binding knows.

response.name: error-envelope-code-case-kept
response.description: Verbatim includes case: a code is not normalised.

response.name: error-envelope-without-message
response.description: A code is what establishes the envelope; an envelope with a code and no message is still one.

response.name: error-envelope-on-a-list
response.description: Error mapping does not depend on the shape of the call that failed.

response.name: error-envelope-on-a-delete
response.description: Nor on a call with no payload to decode.

response.name: bare-404
response.description: A 404 with no Octonomy envelope: a wrong base URL, a path-stripping proxy, a server with no route for this surface. No status is mapped to a code, on either surface -- this is not not_found, and reading it as one turns an infrastructure failure into an empty taxonomy.

response.name: bare-409-empty
response.description: Every status is treated alike without an envelope; a bare 409 is not a conflict.

response.name: bare-401-text
response.description: A gateway's plain-text 401 is not an Octonomy authentication error.

response.name: bare-500-empty
response.description: A 500 with nothing in it.

response.name: error-envelope-without-code
response.description: An error object with no code did not establish one; it is treated as having no envelope.

response.name: body-at-the-ceiling
response.description: A body of exactly 32 MiB (33554432 bytes) is read and decoded. The size is the behaviour: a binding must not substitute a smaller test ceiling here.

response.name: body-over-the-ceiling
response.description: One byte past 32 MiB is refused rather than read without bound or truncated.

response.name: error-body-over-the-ceiling
response.description: A non-2xx whose body is over the ceiling is still an API error, carrying its status, and the size refusal is reachable through it.

response.name: nesting-at-the-limit
response.description: A response nested exactly 10000 levels deep, counting the outermost object as level 1, is decoded. @NEST@ becomes 9997 opening brackets followed by 9997 closing ones.

response.name: nesting-past-the-limit
response.description: One level deeper, 10001, is refused before it is decoded.

response.name: health-ok
response.description: A readiness probe answered with the health view's bare status body, which carries no data envelope.

response.name: health-other-word
response.description: Whatever word the server sends reaches the caller verbatim.

response.name: health-unavailable
response.description: A non-2xx carrying the health view's own status body is not_ready -- established by the body, not inferred from the status.

response.name: health-status-body-on-a-500
response.description: not_ready comes from the body, whatever the non-2xx status: a 500 carrying the health view's status body is not_ready too.

response.name: health-bare-503
response.description: A 503 without that body is no more not_ready than a bare 404 is not_found.

response.name: health-503-empty-object
response.description: A JSON object with no status is not the health view's body.

response.name: health-503-error-envelope
response.description: A probe answered with an Octonomy error envelope keeps that envelope's code, as any call does.

response.name: health-error-body-over-the-ceiling
response.description: The probes read under the same ceiling as the API, by their own request path: an oversized non-2xx probe answer is still an API error, with the size refusal reachable through it.

response.name: health-body-over-the-ceiling
response.description: A 2xx probe over the ceiling is refused like any other 2xx, and is not an API error.

response.name: health-empty-object
response.description: A 2xx whose body names no status must not read as a healthy server.

response.name: health-blank-status
response.description: A status of only whitespace carries no word.

response.name: health-empty-body
response.description: A 2xx probe with no body at all.

request.name: v1-plain-read
request.description: The floor case: an unscoped read on v1 is sent, with no namespace.

request.name: v1-namespace
request.description: /api/v1 is global-only, so a namespace on a v1 client is refused before it is sent, application or no.

request.name: v1-namespaced-create
request.description: The v1 refusal does not depend on the call: a write that names a namespace is refused on v1 too.

request.name: v1-namespace-cancelled
request.description: A namespace cleared by the global-namespace option before the request is built names no namespace, so v1 has nothing to refuse.

request.name: global-namespace-alone
request.description: The global-namespace option on its own sends no namespace, on either surface.

request.name: v2-namespaced-read
request.description: A namespaced read that names its application is sent with both namespace headers and the application in the query.

request.name: v2-namespaced-get
request.description: A namespaced single-resource read that names its application.

request.name: v2-namespaced-delete
request.description: A namespaced delete that names its application: the option is how a bodyless delete names one.

request.name: v2-namespaced-read-application-from-params
request.description: The application may come from the call's own parameters instead of the option.

request.name: v2-namespaced-resolve-application-from-params
request.description: Resolution takes its application from its own parameters too.

request.name: v2-namespaced-read-without-application
request.description: Namespace isolation sits below application on the server, so a namespaced read that names no application is refused.

request.name: v2-namespaced-read-blank-application-param
request.description: An application parameter that is present but blank names no application. Presence is what makes it contradict an option; it is not what satisfies a namespaced read.

request.name: v2-namespaced-get-without-application
request.description: The same holds for a single-resource read, which has no parameters to carry an application.

request.name: v2-namespaced-delete-without-application
request.description: And for a delete: it carries no body, so the query is all the application scope there is.

request.name: v2-namespaced-resolve-without-application
request.description: Resolution is a bodyless read like any other: namespaced, it must name its application.

request.name: v2-namespaced-create
request.description: A write carries its application in its body, which the transport does not inspect; it is sent, and the server decides.

request.name: namespace-type-blank
request.description: A namespace with no type.

request.name: namespace-type-whitespace
request.description: A namespace type of only whitespace names no type.

request.name: namespace-id-blank
request.description: A namespace type with no id: half a pair.

request.name: namespace-type-reserved
request.description: global is the reserved namespace type: the global namespace is selected by sending no namespace at all.

request.name: namespace-type-reserved-is-case-sensitive
request.description: Namespace values are opaque and not case-folded, on the client as on the server: "Global" is an ordinary type, and only "global" is reserved.

request.name: two-namespaces
request.description: Two different namespaces on one request are a contradiction, never last-wins: last-wins on this axis is a cross-merchant read.

request.name: two-namespaces-differing-in-type
request.description: Two namespaces with the same id and different types are as contradictory as two ids.

request.name: same-namespace-twice
request.description: Naming the same namespace twice contradicts nothing.

request.name: namespace-sent-verbatim
request.description: A namespace goes out exactly as written, case included.

request.name: namespace-replaced-through-global
request.description: Clearing a namespace with the global-namespace option is the one way to change it; a different one may follow.

request.name: application-blank
request.description: An application option naming no application.

request.name: two-applications
request.description: Two different applications from two options.

request.name: same-application-twice
request.description: The same application twice contradicts nothing.

request.name: application-contradicts-params
request.description: An application option that contradicts the call's own application parameter.

request.name: application-contradicts-empty-params
request.description: A parameter explicitly set to the empty string is present, so an option naming an application contradicts it rather than filling it in.

request.name: application-agrees-with-params
request.description: An option naming the same application as the call's own parameter contradicts nothing, and the parameter is sent once.

request.name: application-option-on-create
request.description: On a write the body's application is authoritative and the server may drop the query value, so the option is refused rather than sometimes ignored.

request.name: application-option-on-update
request.description: The same for an update.

request.name: v1-include-global
request.description: include_global is meaningful only where a namespace axis exists.

request.name: v2-include-global-on-create
request.description: The server reads include_global only on safe methods and ignores it on a write, so it is refused rather than sent to do nothing.

request.name: v2-include-global-on-update
request.description: The same for an update.

request.name: v2-include-global-on-delete
request.description: And for a delete: it is not a safe method, so the server would not read include_global on it either.

request.name: v2-include-global-without-namespace
request.description: include_global needs a v2 client, not a namespace: on a global read it is sent, and the server decides what it adds.

request.name: v2-namespaced-read-including-global
request.description: A namespaced read that also asks for the global rows.

request.name: merchant-scope-without-namespace
request.description: Resolving within the request's namespace when the request has none, on either surface.

request.name: merchant-scope-with-include-global
request.description: A merchant-pinned resolution excludes global rows by definition; the server would drop include_global in silence.

request.name: global-scope-with-include-global
request.description: A global-pinned resolution alongside include_global is redundant, not contradictory.
